item.title: The Data Imperative for Smart Microfactories
item.description: Microfactories are not just smaller replicas of mega-factories. They operate with radically different assumptions. Data is real-time and transient, not batch-processed. Production is modular, not linear. And, decision-making is distributed, not centralized.

item.title: U.S. Manufacturing Grows in January, Ending Yearlong Contraction
item.description: WASHINGTON— U.S. manufacturing activity grew in January and has returned to expansion for the first time in a year, driven by a sharp rebound in new orders. Factory operators, however, are still navigating higher input costs, labor pressure and supply chain strain.

item.title: Inside BMW’s New State-of-the-Art Assembly Plant
item.description: BMW’s newest assembly plant makes the iX3 electric SUV, the first vehicle based on the automaker’s Neue Klasse platform.

item.title: How Do High-Velocity Impacts Affect Adhesive Bonding?
item.description: This dual experimental-numerical approach provides a rare, holistic view of bonded joint performance under ballistic loading, bridging the critical gap between laboratory testing and real-world service demands.

item.title: AI Use Expands Across Manufacturing, Study Finds, but Scaling Remains Limited
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, Fla.– After years of experimentation, artificial intelligence is now a core priority for manufacturers, but a new study shows that adoption is moving faster than the foundations needed to support it.

item.title: Can Ergonomic Improvements Increase Productivity?
item.description: By optimizing workflow and minimizing strain, ergonomic adjustments can increase efficiency and help employees perform tasks more effectively.

item.title: From Machine Operators to Managers, Manufacturers Shift Hiring Priorities
item.description: ATLANTA— Manufacturers are entering 2026 facing a tightening labor market marked by an aging workforce, persistent skills gaps and hundreds of thousands of unfilled jobs.

item.title: New California Fee Targets Products with Nonremovable Batteries
item.description: SACRAMENTO, Calif.—Products with nonremovable batteries are the target of a new state recycling fee structure in California that expands the state’s electronic waste program, targeting everything from power tools with embedded batteries to video game consoles.

item.title: Precision Assembly and Testing with Electric Torque Control
item.description: Modern manufacturing demands torque accuracy, traceability, and repeatability. The Promess TorquePRO delivers all three with a fully electric, programmable system designed for precision assembly and test applications across every industry.

item.title: Combining Linear and Rotational Precision in One System
item.description: Assembly processes are becoming more complex, and manufacturers need solutions that combine multiple motions without sacrificing accuracy. The Promess REMAP delivers programmable linear and rotational control in a single compact, ready to run unit.
